description: William de Warenne, earl of Surrey to Hubert de Burgh, justiciar: he is forced to call upon de Burgh for money which he and Sir William the Marshal were sureties, since he must pay the earl of Arundel £100 which he owes him at his setting out at Midsummer; and he has likewise long been in de Burgh's debt for the money he lent him in his great affair. He cannot get any help from Jew or Christian, and it was at his request and the Marshal's that he lent the money. He is willing to abate part of the debt in return for prompt payment. He has never pressed de Burgh though in sore straits, for he owes money to the Crusaders which he must repay, and add some of his own as well. £100 now is more than £1000 after Midsummer. Asks him to let him know his purpose by Elias de Marevill and his brother Mainard to whom de Burgh may give credence. He does not have his great seal with him so has sealed with his privy seal.

description: Pandulf, bishop elect of Norwich and legate, to Peter des Roches, bishop of Winchester and Hubert de Burgh, justiciar: he has previously discussed with them the immoderate interest exacted by the Jews contrary to the decrees of the lateran Council. The abbot and convent of Westminster now complain that Isaac of Norwich is suing them for unlawful interest before the Justices of the Jews. Asks them to tell the Justices to adjourn the case until he can come, and the question can be settled. As it was jointly agreed that because of the craft of the sheriffs, associates should be appointed to assist them in levying the amercements, he is surprised to find that they have received a general order to proceed by themselves. They must do as agreed and appoint suitable associates. Walter Mauclerc is to be appointed in the counties of Lincolnshire, Nottinghamshire and Derbyshire. Given at Wenlock and dated the Nones of July.
